name: Chemistry AI & ML Applications
tagline: Machine learning models applied to molecular property prediction and synthesis.
seo_title: Chemistry AI & ML Applications — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Chemistry AI & ML Applications on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in machine learning for property prediction, molecular design, synthesis planning and simulation.

definition.lead: This page covers how machine learning is applied across chemistry: predicting properties, planning syntheses, generating new molecules and speeding up simulations.
definition.body: Models learn patterns from data on molecules and reactions, then make predictions in milliseconds that would take hours of computation or weeks of lab work. The hard parts are good data, honest validation and knowing when a model is out of its depth.

timeline.title: QSAR
timeline.text: Hansch and Fujita fit biological activity to molecular descriptors.
timeline.why: The ancestor of molecular machine learning.

timeline.title: Backpropagation
timeline.text: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams popularize training neural networks by backpropagation.

timeline.title: SMILES
timeline.text: David Weininger publishes a text notation for molecules.
timeline.why: Later used to feed molecules to language models.

timeline.title: Deep learning enters chemistry
timeline.text: A deep neural network team wins Merck's molecular activity challenge on Kaggle.
timeline.why: Drew attention to deep learning for drug discovery.

timeline.title: Message passing
timeline.text: Justin Gilmer and colleagues describe message-passing neural networks for molecules.
timeline.why: A common framework for graph-based chemistry models.

timeline.title: Generating molecules
timeline.text: Rafael Gómez-Bombarelli and colleagues design molecules in a continuous learned space.

timeline.title: An antibiotic found by deep learning
timeline.text: A deep learning screen identifies halicin as an antibacterial candidate.
timeline.why: AI found a structurally unusual antibiotic.

timeline.title: AlphaFold 2 published
timeline.text: The method and a database of predicted protein structures are released.
timeline.why: Structures became available for almost any protein.

timeline.title: Nobel Prizes for AI
timeline.text: The Chemistry prize rewards protein structure prediction and design; the Physics prize, neural network foundations.
timeline.why: AI recognized at the core of science.

quiz.q: Why split data into training, validation and test sets?
options: To estimate how the model performs on data it has never seen
To make training faster
To use less memory
Because the software requires it
quiz.explain: The test set must stay untouched until the end.

quiz.q: A graph neural network represents a molecule as…
options: A graph with atoms as nodes and bonds as edges
An image of its 2D structure drawing
A sentence describing the molecule in words
A single number such as its molar mass
quiz.explain: Information passes along bonds between atoms.

quiz.q: A typical sign of overfitting is…
options: Very low training error but poor test error
Equal training and test error
High error everywhere
No error at all
quiz.explain: The model memorized instead of learning.

options: Turning molecules into numerical inputs for a model
Adding features to software
Drawing molecules
Naming molecules
quiz.explain: Fingerprints, descriptors and graphs are common choices.

quiz.q: Machine-learned interatomic potentials are usually trained on…
options: Quantum chemistry calculations
Only experiments
Pictures of molecules
Patent text
quiz.explain: They learn energies and forces from DFT or higher-level data.

options: A model can only be as good as its data
Models produce garbage
Data must be thrown away
Recycling matters

Reaction yields from the reagents used

quiz.q: Why can random splits mislead in chemistry?
options: Near-identical molecules land in both training and test sets, inflating scores
They are not random enough to be statistically fair
They are too slow for data sets of real size
They throw away part of the data set
quiz.explain: Scaffold or time-based splits are more honest tests.
